header: Problem 8 Analysis of Substituent Effects. This problem compares the magnitudes of -ΔG° for a series of substituents or substrates in the conformational or isomerization reactions shown.

subquestions.text_open:
Reaction (a) below is shared by 8.3–8.6. In 8.3–8.5, compare the shared Reaction (a) with Reaction (b) shown in the corresponding subproblem and select the reaction with the larger -ΔG°.
8.3

text_images.description: Prompt figure for part a: the image shows a change from left to right. On the left is a six-membered ring in a chair conformation with an axial Me group on the right-hand carbon; its SMILES is 'CC1CCCCC1'. A one-way arrow points right. On the right is the same chair-shaped ring with an equatorial Me group on the right-hand carbon; its SMILES is likewise 'CC1CCCCC1'.

Prompt figure for part b: the image shows a change from left to right. On the left is a six-membered ring in a chair conformation bearing a carbonyl (=O) at the lower-left vertex and an axial Me group on the right-hand carbon; its SMILES is 'CC1CC(=O)CCC1'. A one-way arrow points right. On the right is the same chair-shaped ring with the same lower-left carbonyl and an equatorial Me group on the right-hand carbon; its SMILES is likewise 'CC1CC(=O)CCC1'.

subquestions.text_open:
In 8.4, Reaction (b) is a base-catalyzed isomerization.
8.4

text_images.description: The image shows a change from left to right. On the left is a six-membered chair bearing an equatorial tert-butyl group at the lower-left carbon, an axial Me group at the right-hand carbon, and a carbonyl (=O) at the lower-right vertex; its SMILES is 'CC1CCC(CC1=O)C(C)(C)C'. A one-way arrow points right. On the right is the same chair with the equatorial tert-butyl group and lower-right carbonyl unchanged, but with the Me group equatorial; its SMILES is likewise 'CC1CCC(CC1=O)C(C)(C)C'.

text_images.description: Prompt figure for option (b): the image shows a change from left to right. On the left is a six-membered chair bearing an equatorial tert-butyl group at the lower-left carbon, an axial $CHMe_2$ group at the right-hand carbon, and a carbonyl (=O) at the lower-right vertex; its SMILES is 'CC(C)C1CCC(CC1=O)C(C)(C)C'. A one-way arrow points right. On the right is the same chair with the equatorial tert-butyl group and lower-right carbonyl unchanged, but with the $CHMe_2$ group equatorial; its SMILES is likewise 'CC(C)C1CCC(CC1=O)C(C)(C)C'.
